pages.observation: The guide explicitly describes both the player's shortened swing after a parry and boss parry haste when a boss parries the player's attacks. Separate spell names and numeric claims remain source/canonical data.
Parry haste the boss is used as a verb in an expertise and survivability discussion. Preserve the noun family but avoid global verb rewriting.
Parry haste occurs as a noun with a timing explanation; source notes boss parries and incoming damage.
Parry haste occurs in a survival worst-case example and as the related parry-hasting verb; not the same as the Haste Rating stat.
Negative control: generic parry, haste, expertise, and official linked talents occur without parry haste jargon. Avoid single-word glossary entries.
Existing independent healing control: downranking and linked spell names; no new parry-haste rule needed.
Existing independent caster control: proc, uptime, spell links and lists; no new parry-haste rule needed.

crossPageFix.concept: Parry haste is a WoW combat mechanic involving faster next melee swings after a parry; distinct from the generic Parry and Haste stats.
crossPageFix.expectedFrench: parry haste (retained as player jargon rather than a misleading literal 'hâte de parade')
crossPageFix.notes: Glossary entries are locale-scoped en->fr; do not map generic parry/haste, named spells or the parry-hasting verb. Official spell/item names remain ID-based. The browser translator may need grammatical handling around verb contexts.

sourceRisks: Source pages can use parry haste for the player's or the boss's faster next swing; preserve semantics and do not hardcode the actor.
Hyphenated verb parry-hasting and phrases such as to parry-haste require natural French prose translation in browser; noun-only data checks do not certify grammar.
